title: Best Browser Infrastructure for AI Agents (2026): 7 Providers Compared
summary: Picking a production browser provider for AI agents: price, concurrency by plan, regions, self-hosting and the catch, for 7 providers. Checked October 27, 2026.
body_markdown:
**Short answer:** Browser Use (ours) has the lowest browser-hour price of these seven ($0.02, no subscription), and it and KERNEL have the fastest session lifecycle here, about 20 ms apart, with the lead changing between[BrowserArena](https://www.browserarena.ai/?percentile=median&sort=latency&date=2026-10-26) runs. Pick Browserbase for debugging, Steel or Browserless to self-host, Anchor for per-task pricing, and Hyperbrowser for one credit pool across browsers, sandboxes and web APIs. For stealth scores and fleet costs, see our[cloud browser comparison](https://browser-use.com/cloud-browsers) .


We make Browser Use. Every price, limit and region below is from the provider's own pricing page, docs or repo, checked October 27, 2026, and linked in the table.

## What to check before you pick


- **Cost per finished task** , not per hour: minimum billing, proxy GB, per-browser fees and retries.
- **Concurrency and create rate** : a burst of tasks needs both.
- **Site access** : stealth, proxies and CAPTCHA solving decide whether the agent gets in.
- **Session cap** : a long task dies at the plan's limit.
- **Region** : put the browser near your agent; every action is a round trip.


## Where each one fits, and the catch


### 1. Browser Use


- **Fits:** agents that need stealth at the lowest hourly price, with[residential proxies in 195+ countries](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/stealth) . Drive them over[CDP with Playwright or Puppeteer](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) , or run[Browser Use agents](https://browser-use.com/web-agents) on the same browsers.
- **Catch:** sessions end at[4 hours](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/api-v4/browsers/create-browser-session) . Closing CDP does not stop the browser; stop it through the API, or it bills until it times out.


### 2. KERNEL


- **Fits:** latency-bound agents, and agents that disconnect while they wait: with no CDP, WebDriver or Live View client connected for 5 seconds, a browser goes into[standby](https://kernel.sh/docs/browsers/standby) and stops billing (not GPU browsers).[Managed Auth](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/info/pricing) is included on every plan, 3 connections on the free one.
- **Catch:** an agent that holds its CDP connection open never goes into standby, and standby browsers still hold a[concurrency slot](https://kernel.sh/docs/browsers/concurrency-and-limits) . Regions, BYO proxies and GPU need the $200/month Start-Up plan. Compare:[Browser Use vs KERNEL](https://browser-use.com/alternatives/kernel) .


### 3. Browserbase


- **Fits:** teams that debug a lot:[live view, replays, logs](https://www.browserbase.com/observability) , and four regions including Singapore.[Stagehand](https://www.stagehand.dev/) is its agent framework.
- **Catch:** sessions end at 15 minutes on Free and 6 hours on Developer and Startup. Verified stealth needs the contact-sales Scale plan ([plans](https://docs.browserbase.com/account/billing/plans) ).


> For a closer look at pricing, stealth, performance, and developer tooling, see[Browser Use vs Browserbase](https://browser-use.com/posts/browser-use-vs-browserbase) .


### 4. Steel


- **Fits:** you must run browsers on your own machines.
- **Catch:** cloud sessions end at 15 minutes on Launch and 1 hour on Scale; browsers run only in us-east. On Launch, CAPTCHA solving and Steel proxies need a $10 deposit ([pricing](https://docs.steel.dev/overview/pricinglimits) ).


### 5. Browserless


- **Fits:** existing[Puppeteer or Playwright](https://browser-use.com/posts/playwright-vs-selenium-vs-puppeteer) scripts, and Firefox or WebKit.
- **Catch:** sessions end at 2, 15, 30 or 60 minutes by plan, a reconnect costs a fresh unit, and each CAPTCHA solve costs 10 units ([pricing](https://www.browserless.io/pricing) ).


> For a detailed comparison of pricing, browser support, and deployment options, see[Browser Use vs Browserless](https://browser-use.com/posts/browser-use-vs-browserless) .


### 6. Anchor


- **Fits:** per-run[task pricing](https://docs.anchorbrowser.io/pricing) : a failed run pays no task fee. Authenticated browsers for third-party logins start on Starter.
- **Catch:** the $0.01 per-browser fee adds up on many short sessions; full stealth and non-US regions start at $2,000/month ([pricing](https://docs.anchorbrowser.io/pricing) ).


### 7. Hyperbrowser


- **Fits:** teams that also need sandboxes or web data APIs: one plan's credits cover browsers, sandboxes, web data and agents ([pricing](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/pricing) ).
- **Catch:** Free runs 1 browser at a time on 5,000 credits; Ultra Stealth is Enterprise only ([pricing](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/pricing) ).


## What browser infrastructure is


A managed service that runs browsers for your agent or script: it starts them, keeps them alive, handles crashes, and gives you a[Chrome DevTools Protocol](https://browser-use.com/posts/what-is-chrome-devtools-protocol) or WebDriver URL to connect to. You start a session through an API, connect, run the task, and stop the session.


Test your shortlist on your own sites before committing: a provider that gets through one site may get blocked on the next.
